title: mecha deus [LORA/Illustrious]
description:
ENGLISH

I built m3ch4 d3us around a religion of engineering: a photorealistic cathedral-forge where priest-pilots maintain giant mecha-saints to repel demonic hordes. War becomes liturgy, maintenance becomes prayer, and each machine is imagined as a martyr's namesake. The images show the installation without its inhabitants: the mechs are inert machines at rest, and the enemy exists only through old damage and sealed defenses.

The set contains 45 square backgrounds: eleven locations with four camera setups each, plus a plunging crane-view synthesis of the nave. Sanctified steel, tarnished gold and ceremonial engineering connect the spaces. A small brass oil can with a mechanical cruciform handle is the recurring detail. I designed each image as an empty stage with a broad open center for adding a character.

Locations:

- Main nave-hangar of kneeling mechs

- Launch choir beneath the rose window

- Holy forge

- Weapons sacristy

- Crypt of

ENGLISH

I imagined a warship with a second life: between battles, its hangar becomes a concert hall. With 1d0l sh1p, I bring matte military grey armor together with flamboyant 1980s retrofuturistic stage lighting, glowing backstage mirrors and the quiet machinery of a working space vessel.

I built this background concept around eleven spaces: the concert bay, dressing rooms, rehearsal studio, recording studio, bridge, crew mess, crew quarters, fighter bay, observation lounge, engine room and spotlight dock. A final exterior view brings the whole vessel together against a nebula.

These are backgrounds only. I express the showbiz glamour through lighting, materials and decor: costumes hang on racks, stages wait in light, fighters remain parked and bunks are neatly made. The intended scenes contain no people or mannequins, no brands or franchise references, and no readable text; displays use abstract light patterns.
